issues.description: Credit card details stored in plain text in PaymentDetails interface. Sensitive payment information should never be held in memory or transmitted without encryption. This violates PCI DSS compliance requirements.
issues.suggestion: Remove storing full card numbers. Only accept tokenized payment data from a secure payment processor (Stripe, Square, etc.). Never handle raw card data in your application. Store only the last 4 digits for display purposes.

issues.description: Card number validation is insufficient - only checks length without validating the Luhn algorithm. This allows invalid card numbers to pass validation and be processed.
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm validation: function isValidCardNumber(cardNumber: string): boolean { const digits = cardNumber.replace(/\D/g, ''); if (digits.length < 13) return false; let sum = 0, isEven = false; for (let i = digits.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { let digit = parseInt(digits[i], 10); if (isEven) digit *= 2; if (digit > 9) digit -= 9; sum += digit; isEven = !isEven; } return sum % 10 === 0; }

issues.description: Card expiry date validation has a Y2K-like bug. Using 'new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1)' means cards valid until 2099 will be treated as expired in year 2100. For 2-digit years, this assumes 2000-2099 range.
issues.suggestion: Determine century based on current year context: const currentYear = new Date().getFullYear(); const century = currentYear > 2000 ? 2000 : 1900; const fullYear = century + parseInt(year); OR better: use a payment processor that handles this complexity.

issues.description: Expired card check is incorrect - it should check if expiry is in the PAST, but creating a Date with month-1 and not setting the day means comparisons may be off by a month. For example, a card expiring 12/25 creates Dec 1, 2025 00:00, which may be before today's date even if card is valid through Dec 31, 2025.
issues.suggestion: Set expiry to the last day of the expiry month: const expiryDate = new Date(fullYear, parseInt(month), 0); // Last day of previous month. This ensures cards are valid through the entire expiry month.

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in chargeCard function. While using parameterized queries for the INSERT, the function doesn't validate that 'amount' is a valid number, potentially allowing injection if the query construction is changed in future.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit validation: if (typeof amount !== 'number' || amount <= 0 || !Number.isFinite(amount)) { throw new Error('Invalid amount'); } before passing to query.

issues.description: Generic error handling with console.error. Payment failures are silently logged but not properly tracked. This makes debugging payment issues difficult and prevents proper error notifications to users.
issues.suggestion: Implement structured error logging and retry logic: catch (error) { logger.error('Payment charge failed', { userId, amount, error }); if (isRetryable(error)) { return retryCharge(payment, amount); } throw error; }

issues.description: Unsafe JSON.parse at line 134 without error handling. If subscription.features contains malformed JSON, this will throw an unhandled exception, potentially crashing the application.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch: const features = (() => { try { return JSON.parse(subscription.features); } catch { logger.warn('Invalid features JSON', { userId, features: subscription.features }); return []; } })();

issues.description: Unsafe JSON.parse at line 161 without error handling. If stored features JSON is corrupted, this will crash. No fallback for malformed data.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: const features = (() => { try { return JSON.parse(row.features); } catch (e) { logger.warn('Failed to parse subscription features', { userId }); return []; } })();

issues.description: Hardcoded subscription tier feature lists are duplicated and scattered. Tier configuration should be centralized to avoid inconsistencies when features are added or modified.
issues.suggestion: Create a tier configuration object: const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes', 'api_access', 'team_collaboration'] }; then use: const features = TIER_FEATURES[tier];

issues.description: Regex pattern is using escaped backslashes (\\/) which is confusing. While technically correct, it reduces readability.
issues.suggestion: Use raw string or simpler pattern: const expiryRegex = /^(0[1-9]|1[0-2])\/\d{2}$/; Or validate programmatically for clarity.

issues.description: Pricing calculation happens on every payment. If this involves currency conversion or tax lookups in future, repeated calls could be inefficient. Currently acceptable but not optimal for scaling.
issues.suggestion: Consider caching tier pricing with memoization or storing in a configuration: const TIER_PRICING = { premium: 9.99, enterprise: 49.99 }; const TAX_RATE = 0.08; // Load from config/database

issues.description: Database queries use raw string SQL. While parameterized queries are used correctly here, the codebase would benefit from an abstraction layer or query builder to reduce duplication.
issues.suggestion: Consider using a query builder library (Knex.js, Prisma, TypeORM) or create a repository layer to encapsulate database operations and reduce SQL string duplication across the file.

issues.description: The validation functions don't use early returns consistently and have multiple return statements spread throughout the function. This reduces readability.
issues.suggestion: Refactor validatePaymentDetails to fail fast with early returns for each validation step: if (cardNumber.length !== 16) return false; if (!isValidCardNumber(cardNumber)) return false; etc.

codeQuality.summary: This payment processing file has critical security vulnerabilities related to storing sensitive credit card data in plain text, insufficient card validation, and unhandled JSON parsing errors. The code handles payment logic without test coverage and contains bugs in expiry date validation logic. The architecture violates PCI DSS compliance by handling raw card numbers.

testCoverage.summary: This critical payment processing module has zero test coverage. All six exported and internal functions are untested, including security-sensitive card validation, payment processing, pricing calculations, and feature access control. The absence of tests for financial transactions, subscription management, and access control represents a critical risk to data integrity and business logic correctness.

suggestions.description: Extract tax and processing fee calculations into separate functions for better reusability and testability. Currently these calculations are inline and hard to test independently.
suggestions.benefits: Each calculation can be tested independently, making the financial logic more maintainable and easier to verify for correctness.

suggestions.description: Extract feature set mapping into a separate function. Currently the tier-to-features mapping is embedded in the subscription upgrade logic.
suggestions.benefits: Feature mappings become a single source of truth, easier to maintain and extend when adding new tiers or features.

suggestions.description: Simplify the validation logic by reducing multiple sequential if-return statements. Early returns make the code harder to follow; consolidate validations.
suggestions.benefits: More declarative validation checks with meaningful variable names make the logic clearer and easier to debug.

suggestions.description: Improve error handling by logging more context and avoid swallowing errors silently. Use nullish coalescing or optional chaining for safer property access.
suggestions.benefits: Safer error logging prevents potential issues when error is not an Error object. Better type safety.

suggestions.description: Create a configuration object to centralize tier-based pricing and features. This follows the Strategy pattern and makes the code more maintainable and extensible.
suggestions.benefits: Single source of truth for tier configuration eliminates duplication, makes adding new tiers easier, and improves code organization.

suggestions.description: Rename the comment 'Simulate payment gateway call' is misleading since this actually performs a real database insert. The function should be more explicit about what it does.
suggestions.benefits: More accurate documentation reduces confusion about whether this is a mock or real implementation.

refactorings.summary: This file has significant refactoring opportunities focused on reducing duplication and improving maintainability. The main issues are scattered tier configuration data (pricing and features), overly verbose validation logic, and financial calculations that are difficult to test independently. Extracting a central tier configuration following the Strategy pattern would eliminate duplication and make the code more extensible. Additionally, simplifying the validation logic with clearer variable names and extracting financial calculations would improve testability and clarity.

recommendations.description: URGENT: Remove storage of plaintext credit card data (cardNumber, CVV, expiryDate in PaymentDetails interface). This violates PCI DSS compliance. Migrate to tokenized payment processing using Stripe, Square, or similar. Never handle raw card data in this application.

Add comprehensive test suite for premium.ts. All 6 functions and all code paths are untested (0% coverage). Critical gaps include payment processing, card validation, pricing calculations, and access control. Implement tests for 35+ identified test cases.

Implement Luhn algorithm validation for credit card numbers. Current length-only validation allows invalid card numbers to be processed. Add validation function and call it from validatePaymentDetails.

Fix card expiry date validation bugs: (1) Y2K-like bug with 2-digit years assumes 2000-2099 range, (2) Expiry check is off by a month due to incorrect Date construction. Set expiry to last day of month and validate against current date properly.
Add error handling for unsafe JSON.parse calls at lines 136 and 149. Malformed JSON in features field will crash the application. Wrap in try-catch with fallback to empty array and logging.

Refactor payment-related configurations into a centralized TIER_CONFIG object following the Strategy pattern. Eliminates duplication of pricing and features, makes code maintainable for adding new tiers.

Improve error logging and handling in chargeCard function. Currently payment failures are silently logged to console. Implement structured logging with context (userId, amount) and consider retry logic for transient failures.
Simplify validatePaymentDetails logic by using more declarative variable names and consolidating validation checks. Current approach with multiple early returns is hard to follow and maintain.
Replace raw SQL queries with an abstraction layer (ORM like Prisma/TypeORM or query builder like Knex.js). Reduces duplication, improves type safety, and makes database operations easier to test.
Add explicit validation for the 'amount' parameter in chargeCard function. Ensure it's a positive finite number before passing to database query to prevent potential injection vulnerabilities.
